name: Colt Technology Services
evidence_summary: Colt sources evidence SD-WAN & SASE, data sovereignty positioning and managed/co-managed service with management portal access.
cost_model: Quote-based managed service; access, SD-WAN/SASE design, data sovereignty and service options drive pricing.
key_differentiators: SD-WAN and SASE with strong European data sovereignty positioning.
Managed and co-managed delivery options with management portal access.
Enterprise-grade connectivity heritage with substantial European network ownership.
best_fit_for: European enterprises prioritising data residency, sovereignty and regulatory alignment.
Buyers wanting genuine co-managed delivery rather than pure managed or pure DIY.
Organisations consolidating European connectivity with SD-WAN under one provider.
watch_outs: Global delivery depth outside Europe is less prominent than the largest global carriers.
CASB and DLP have partial public evidence; SSE platform partner choice should be confirmed.
Underlying SD-WAN platform should be explicitly confirmed in RFP.
verification_notes: Re-verified 2026-07-29 against named primary sources. Every graded fact carries a source, a tier and a verbatim quote confirmed present on the cited page by an independent check. Industry, region, organisation-size and pricing evidence was sourced on the same basis. Facts that could not be sourced are published as unknown with the reason. The value_tier field is a Netify assessment of relative cost position, not a supplier claim: most of this market publishes no price. Sources found and rejected are listed at tier 4.

ai_capability.note: Depends on vendor platform (Versa, VeloCloud); Colt On Demand portal adds analytics.

resilience.note: Owned Colt IQ Network fibre with diverse routing and on-demand failover.

profile.platform_architecture: Colt delivers managed SD-WAN over the Colt IQ Network: dense owned metro fibre across European business districts plus strong Asian reach, now extended by the Lumen EMEA acquisition. Platform options centre on Versa and VeloCloud, with Colt On Demand bringing genuine NaaS behaviour: bandwidth flexing and service changes from a portal in near real time.
profile.security_sase: Managed SASE pairs the SD-WAN platforms with partner SSE (Versa's stack and Zscaler pairings) plus managed security operations. Depth follows the platform; Colt's distinctive contribution is the quality of the underlay and the on-demand operating model rather than first-party security IP.
profile.service_support_channel: Fully managed and co-managed with 24x7 operations, UK support desks and named service management; capital markets and financial services delivery is a Colt signature, including ultra-low-latency heritage. European city coverage on owned fibre keeps delivery predictable.
profile.commercials_verdict: Per-site managed pricing with On Demand consumption options, quote based. The Netify verdict: shortlist Colt for Europe-led estates concentrated in major cities, financial services networks valuing owned-fibre determinism, and buyers attracted to portal-driven bandwidth flexing. Estates needing deep US or rest-of-world delivery should weigh the expanded but still Europe-first footprint.

vendor_faqs.q: What does Colt On Demand actually let me change?
vendor_faqs.a: Bandwidth and service characteristics from a portal with near real-time effect on the Colt IQ Network, which suits seasonal or project-driven estates and avoids contract variation cycles for routine changes.

vendor_faqs.q: Why do financial services firms favour Colt?
vendor_faqs.a: Owned metro fibre into the buildings that matter, low-latency heritage between trading venues, and managed services shaped by two decades of serving capital markets across European and Asian financial centres.

vendor_faqs.q: How does the Lumen EMEA acquisition change Colt?
vendor_faqs.a: It adds network reach, infrastructure and customers across EMEA, deepening Colt's footprint beyond its metro strongholds. Integration is ongoing; ask for current coverage maps during procurement.

shortlist_summary: Colt offer SD-WAN and SASE with a European data sovereignty positioning that's hard to match from a carrier without Colt's owned fibre network across European business districts. Typically shortlisted by EU-headquartered organisations or those with compliance requirements around in-region data processing, where sovereignty isn't just a preference but a hard procurement filter.
cost_note: Per-site managed with on-demand bandwidth flexing; mid pricing on owned European fibre.
uk_basis: UK headquartered (London). UK contracting entity with owned UK metro fibre and UK support.

evidence_register.title: Colt Technology Services expands its capital markets offering into Latin America - Telecom Ramblings newswire
evidence_register.reliability: Newswire republication of the supplier press release. Corroboration only; carries no independent reporting and does not carry a grade alone.

evidence_register.title: Colt Technology Services: European Fibre Network and SD-WAN | Netify
evidence_register.reliability: Not used as evidence. This is Netify's own existing marketplace profile, which is the very content this exercise is replacing, so citing it would be circular. It asserts pricing geared to enterprise rather than SMB and 220+ metro networks across 31 countries, none of which is independently sourced on the page.

f01_fully_managed_service.quote: Our Next Generation Firewall is fully managed by Colt, and offers perimeter security, application awareness and content security, including IDS/IPS, anti-malware, URL filtering and SSL inspection.
f01_fully_managed_service.note: Colt states outright that it fully manages the firewall element and provides 24x7 proactive management, monitoring and reporting. The SD-WAN service guide describes Colt managed CPE and zero touch provisioning. Confidence is medium rather than high because the strongest 'fully managed' wording sits on the cybersecurity page and covers the security service, not an end-to-end SD-WAN managed tier; no page found publishes a named fully managed SD-WAN service level.

f03_co_managed_service.quote: Customers can choose to do (add/edit/delete) all their policy configurations anytime via the secure Colt SD WAN portal
f03_co_managed_service.note: This is a textbook shared-responsibility split: Colt runs the platform, CPE and support while the customer retains live policy and change rights through the portal. The guide also states customers can add branch sites in hours and upgrade bandwidth in real time themselves.

f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.quote: For the Wholesale SD WAN service, both wholesale customers and end customers will benefit from a customized look and feel, setting wholesale customer's own logo, background image, links and contact details, so that their end-customer experience doesn't differ from the rest of their services offered.
f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.note: All four elements of the definition are evidenced on one page: branded portal (logo, background, links), delegated administration (the carrier holds end-customer credentials and handles resets), tenant isolation (IPC* tenant identifiers in Versa Director) and hierarchy templates (customizable portal, branding and further hierarchy levels). Colt sells this explicitly as a Wholesale SD WAN solution for partners to resell.

f05_professional_services_and_migration_.quote: Project Management – End-to-end project management services for the implementation of the services
f05_professional_services_and_migration_.note: Colt publishes a professional services portfolio covering consultancy, service integration, project management, service induction (training) and end-to-end workload migrations. Graded partial rather than yes because the definition requires structured discovery, pilots, staging, migration runbooks and rollback plans, and none of the words discovery, pilot, staging, runbook or rollback appear on the professional services page. The migration wording found is about cloud workload migration, not WAN or SD-WAN migration.

f07_lifecycle_management.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. I searched the SD-WAN external service guide and the SD-WAN datasheet specifically for hardware replacement, spares, RMA, firmware upgrade, software upgrade, patching, renewals and end-of-life, and the service guide fetch returned an explicit negative on all of those terms. The guide does contain planned works and maintenance headings, but no published statement that hardware replacement, patching or end-of-life planning is included in the service. Absence of a statement is not evidence of absence of the capability.

f17_cellular_and_5g_support.quote: Colt SD WAN services can be provided over public internet – broadband Internet and business internet – dedicated internet access (DIA) connectivity (using any and all transport technologies like xDSL, wireless 3G/4G/LTE/5G (only available in EU for Colt provided SIMs, no limitation for customer-owned), Ethernet or traditional MPLS regardless of whether Colt is providing that underlying connectivity or not.
f17_cellular_and_5g_support.note: 4G and 5G are supported as transport, and SIM management is evidenced both ways: Colt provided SIMs (EU only) or customer-owned SIMs with no geographic limitation. A separate wireless option is delivered with Blue Wireless, a Singapore-based company, supplying a Cradlepoint mobile router with dual SIM, data, installation, operation and an SLA. Confidence is medium because the guide also states that by default 3G/4G/5G circuits should be used as backup only where fixed Internet and MPLS are available, and because no published evidence of signal monitoring was found. Note the sentence quoted is reproduced as printed, including its unclosed parenthesis and en dashes.

f19_public_cloud_gateways.quote: The SASE services can be deployed via the cloud and/or on-premises; Colt is deploying the Versa SWG plus other Versa services via the Versa Operating System (VOS) within Colt's own cloud.
f19_public_cloud_gateways.note: Split verdict, and the distinction matters. Colt does operate its own gateway infrastructure: the SASE security enforcement runs inside Colt's own cloud, and the service guide states Colt has deployed multiple Cloud Gateways in Europe and Asia for AWS, Microsoft and Google connectivity. However the enforcement software riding those gateways is Versa's, not Colt's, and the guide offers a parallel Versa SDWAN with Zscaler SSE option where the enforcement PoPs belong entirely to Zscaler. Graded partial rather than yes on that mixed ownership, and not partner_integrated because the hosting infrastructure in the primary option is genuinely Colt's. Per the definition I have discounted the AWS/Azure/GCP connectivity gateways as evidence in themselves. Best quote comes from Tier 2 journalism because Colt's own pages do not state where the gateways are hosted.

f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.quote: Sovereign SASE keeps data within its own network and in specific regions, avoiding third-party transfers and boosting control.
f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.note: Colt markets a Sovereign SASE deployment model and a Versa Hosted SASE Solution, and the product page describes sovereign SASE as a model where the organisation or a service provider hosts all components. That evidences regional and sovereign data control. Graded partial rather than yes because no page found describes a customer-hosted or single-tenant dedicated PoP as an orderable option with defined commercials; the published claim is about data residency within Colt's own network, which is not the same as a dedicated PoP.

f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.note: The service guide publishes a contractual availability SLA differentiated by site package, 99.90% for XS/S/M/L and 99.95% for the S Plus, M Plus and L Plus tiers, and the guide is a service-guide-grade document rather than marketing. The wireless option is separately stated to guarantee 50% of contract speed. Confidence is medium on two counts: the SLA applies to on-net circuits only, and no published response-time, change-handling, latency, jitter or loss commitments were found. The quote is a table row, so a verifier should expect it rendered as a table rather than prose.

f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.quote: Our Next Generation Firewall is fully managed by Colt, and offers perimeter security, application awareness and content security, including IDS/IPS, anti-malware, URL filtering and SSL inspection.
f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.note: Every element the definition requires is present and it is genuinely built into the platform rather than bolted on: the service guide states the Colt SD WAN platform uses an integrated Next Generation firewall integrated with the SD-WAN router, with Basic (Layer 3/4 stateful) and Advanced (Layer 7 policies, DDoS) tiers, and Versa CPE firewall session logs covering Security Policy, URL/IP Filtering, DOS, IPS, AntiVirus and Decryption. Graded partner_integrated and not yes because the technology is not Colt's: the datasheet states Colt has supplier partnerships with a range of vendors, including Versa Networks, Cisco, Meraki, Aruba, Fortinet, Palo Alto, Juniper and VMware, and the SD-WAN NGFW is Versa's.

f33_data_loss_prevention.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. I searched the SD-WAN and SASE external service guide, the cybersecurity solutions page, the managed security page, the security support page and the cybersecurity services datasheet for DLP, data loss prevention, CASB and content classification. The service guide fetch returned an explicit negative: DLP and Data Loss Prevention do not appear anywhere in that document. Versa Networks, the underlying SASE vendor, does market a Network DLP product, but that is the vendor's claim and not a Colt-published capability, so it cannot carry this grade. If Colt does resell Versa DLP the correct grade would be partner_integrated, but no Colt page states it.

f40_managed_service_assurance.quote: Our managed security services are managed by highly specialized engineers and analysts in Colt's Cyber Security Operations Centers (CSOC) across Asia and Europe.
f40_managed_service_assurance.note: The monitoring half of the definition is well evidenced: Colt publishes 24x7 proactive management, monitoring, and reporting, staffed CSOCs across Asia and Europe, a named Security Operations Center support route, and near real time interactive dashboards in the SD-WAN portal. Change governance is partly evidenced through the guide's Modifying an Existing Service and Out-of-hours Changes sections. Graded partial rather than yes because the definition is compound and two elements are missing from public sources: no published commitment to owning incidents through to root cause analysis, and no description of structured service reviews.

delivery_model.quote: Our managed security services are managed by highly specialized engineers and analysts in Colt's Cyber Security Operations Centers (CSOC) across Asia and Europe.
delivery_model.note: Colt operates services on its own fibre network and manages third-party SD-WAN and security technology. It does not author the SD-WAN or SSE stack: the datasheet lists Versa Networks, Cisco, Meraki, Aruba, Fortinet, Palo Alto, Juniper and VMware as supplier partners. Graded managed_provider rather than both because no Colt-authored SD-WAN or SSE product was found.

underlay_ownership.quote: Colt SD WAN services can be provided over public internet – broadband Internet and business internet – dedicated internet access (DIA) connectivity (using any and all transport technologies like xDSL, wireless 3G/4G/LTE/5G (only available in EU for Colt provided SIMs, no limitation for customer-owned), Ethernet or traditional MPLS regardless of whether Colt is providing that underlying connectivity or not.
underlay_ownership.note: Unambiguously mixed, and the supplier says so itself in the closing clause: regardless of whether Colt is providing that underlying connectivity or not. Colt genuinely owns substantial physical infrastructure (50+ metropolitan area networks across 230+ cities, 10 submarine cable systems, a fully redundant network core) and also states that Colt SD WAN supports Colt provided MPLS underlay connection as a standard. But the same service equally rides third-party broadband, DIA and customer-owned circuits and SIMs.

sse_layer_ownership.quote: Colt has supplier partnerships with a range of vendors, including Versa Networks, Cisco, Meraki, Aruba, Fortinet, Palo Alto, Juniper and VMware.
sse_layer_ownership.note: Versa Networks is the primary SSE partner. Colt's own service guide offers a Versa Hosted SASE Solution and an alternative Versa SDWAN with Zscaler SSE Solution, and the 2022 press release describes the integrated full SASE offering as underpinned by Colt's long-standing partnership with Versa Networks, including Versa Secure Web Gateway. Light Reading confirms Colt deploys Versa SWG and other Versa services via the Versa Operating System within Colt's own cloud. Colt's security portfolio page additionally names Fortinet, Zscaler and Palo Alto. Graded partner rather than resold because Colt hosts and operates the primary stack on its own infrastructure rather than simply reselling a vendor's tenancy. No Colt-authored SSE technology was found. Vendors named: Versa Networks (primary), Zscaler, Fortinet, Palo Alto.

regulatory_documentation.note: Colt publishes a technical certifications page naming specific standards with version years, which meets the documented bar rather than assurance_only. Frameworks found: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (Information Security Management), ISO/IEC 27701:2019 (Privacy Information Management System), ISO 9001:2015, ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 22301:2019 (Business Continuity Management), Cyber Essentials and Cyber Essentials Plus, Binding Corporate Rules, and a Certificate of compliance with the National Security Scheme (ENS, Spain). Frameworks explicitly NOT found on that page: SOC 2, NHS DSPT, DORA, NIS2, PCI DSS and TISAX. Given Colt is an EU and UK telecoms operator, the absence of any published NIS2 or DORA positioning is worth flagging to a buyer in a regulated sector.

pop_count.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. Colt does not publish a count of its own SASE or SD-WAN points of presence. The nearest published figure on the global network page is 250+ connected cloud PoPs worldwide, but those are third-party cloud provider on-ramps that Colt connects to, not Colt-operated PoPs, so using it as a PoP count would misrepresent the estate. The SD-WAN service guide refers only to Multiple points of presence with no number attached, and states Colt has deployed multiple Cloud Gateways in Europe and Asia without quantifying them. Related published scale figures, which are not PoP counts: 40+ countries connected, 230+ cities connected with 50+ MANs, 1,100+ Data Centres.

sla_availability_pct.note: 99.90% is the baseline availability across the XS, S, M and L site packages; the S Plus, M Plus and L Plus packages carry 99.95%. I have recorded the baseline as the headline value since it applies to the majority of tiers. Two caveats for a buyer: the figure is qualified as applying to on-net circuits only, so off-net and internet-underlay sites are not covered by it, and the value is published in a table rather than prose, so the quote is a table row. No availability percentage appears on any of Colt's marketing-facing SD-WAN or SASE pages.

sectors.healthcare.quote: SD WAN with Cloud Access and Secure Enterprise Gateway (Zscaler)
sectors.healthcare.note: Colt publishes a healthcare-labelled SD-WAN case study titled "Leading provider of medical devices in the global healthcare sector", where the stated solution is SD WAN with Cloud Access and Secure Enterprise Gateway (Zscaler) alongside Colt Intelligent Communications and Colt Professional Services. The customer is anonymised, so there is no named healthcare reference. There is no healthcare industry page: /solutions/industries/healthcare returns 404 and healthcare is absent from both the six-item industries hub and the eight-item resources industry filter. Graded yes on the strength of a sector-labelled, SD-WAN-specific case study, but a buyer should note the anonymity.

sectors.financial_services.quote: 18/25 of the top global banks trust us with their critical infrastructure and connectivity
sectors.financial_services.note: Dedicated Capital Markets industry page with named customers Stuttgart Stock Exchange, Byblos Bank Europe and RCI Bank and Services. Byblos Bank Europe is quoted on a Colt and Zscaler SSE deployment: "Compared to our previous VPN-based approach, the Colt and Zscaler solution is a real enhancement that delivers a faster and better user experience and helps increase productivity" (Ramy Matar, Network Consultant, BBE). Note the focus is capital markets and trading connectivity rather than retail banking or insurance; the 18/25 top global banks figure is a vendor claim with no source cited on the page.

sectors.retail_ecommerce.quote: With Colt we have a reliable networking solution that meets our simplification and consolidation aims. It also allows us to centralise our billing & optimise our costs across Europe.
sectors.retail_ecommerce.note: Dedicated Retail industry page carrying attributed customer quotes, including the one cited from Thomas Laromiguiere, IT Systems Architect, RRG (Renault Retail Group). Decathlon appears as a named customer on both the Manufacturing and Enterprise pages. Caution: the retail page renders speaker names and job titles concatenated without separating punctuation, so the attribution line may not match a naive string search.

sectors.energy_utilities.quote: INEOS is a leading global petrochemicals manufacturer made up of 36 individual businesses which touch every aspect of modern-day life.
sectors.energy_utilities.note: No energy or utilities evidence found. Checked: the industries hub, which lists only Capital Markets, Manufacturing, Pharma, Retail, Transport & Logistics and Defence; the resources library industry filter, which adds only Media & Entertainment and Professional services; and the customer stories index. The nearest adjacency is INEOS, a petrochemicals group, but Colt labels that story Manufacturing, not energy. No utility, grid, oil and gas or renewables customer, page or accreditation was found. Do not infer energy capability from the petrochemicals reference.

sectors.education.quote: Esade is a globally recognised academic institution, delivering top-tier education to over 15,000 students each year — 40% of whom are international.
sectors.education.note: Esade is a named customer with a Colt customer story dated 6 November 2025 that Colt labels Education, and it also appears on the mid-market segment page. This is a single named reference: there is no education industry page and education is not in the resources industry filter list. The solutions listed on the Esade story are IP Access and infrastructure network services, not SD-WAN or SASE, so this evidences sector reach rather than SD-WAN delivery into education.

sectors.transport_logistics.quote: Colt's high-bandwidth cloud connectivity service has made it possible for us to transmit large volumes of reservation and ticketing data to our analytics system quickly and reliably.
sectors.transport_logistics.note: Dedicated Transport & Logistics industry page listing SD WAN + SASE among its networking services. Named customers with attributed quotes: All Nippon Airways (quoted, Takahiro Morishita, Manager, Information Security & IT Architecture Strategy), Cosco Shipping Lines (Johan De Wispelaere, IT Manager) and Eurovision (Graham Warren, Network Director). Brussels Airlines also appears in the logo set. The named engagements are cloud connectivity and voice rather than SD-WAN specifically.

sectors.professional_services.quote: The Singapore and Tokyo offices of Arthur D. Little have recently been migrated to Colt's network.
sectors.professional_services.note: Professional services is one of the eight industry filter categories in Colt's resources library, and Arthur D. Little, a global management consultancy, is named as a Colt customer both on Colt's mid-market segment page and in dated trade journalism from November 2020. Caveats: the published Arthur D. Little engagement is SIP trunking and business internet in Singapore and Japan, not SD-WAN or SASE; there is no professional services industry page; and the third-party report is nearly six years old. Altares and CoStar Group also appear as named mid-market customers but with no sector-labelled story behind them.

sectors.hospitality_leisure.quote: We turned to Colt because it has good availability of proprietary fibre in all the main countries where lm group operates.
sectors.hospitality_leisure.note: Evidence is indirect and conflicting. The quoted line is from Giuseppe Arcoraci, Network Manager at lm group (the lastminute.com online travel group), but it sits on Colt's Retail page rather than a hospitality page. Kinepolis, an international cinema and entertainment group with 122 cinemas, has a Colt customer story dated 23 April 2026, but Colt labels it Media & Entertainment and the solution is Network as a Service, not SD-WAN. Classik Business Space of the Classik Hotel Collection GmbH is listed among named customers on the mid-market page, but no hotel case study page was located. There is no hospitality or leisure industry page and no such filter in the resources library. Graded partial, not yes, because every reference is sector-adjacent or sector-mislabelled and none is a hospitality-labelled case study.

regions.uk_ireland.quote: establishes Edinburgh and Glasgow as the 53rd and 54th Colt Metro Cities
regions.uk_ireland.note: Colt was founded in London and lists London as HQ plus a Dublin office. UK metro delivery is documented through the CityFibre partnership extending on-net reach into Leeds, Bristol, Slough, Bracknell, Reading, Milton Keynes, Edinburgh and Glasgow, taking Colt to 54 metro cities. Independently corroborated by the live UK G-Cloud 14 listing for Colt SD-WAN, which is a UK-sold, UK-priced service with PSN certification. Ireland evidence is thinner than UK evidence: a Dublin office is listed but no Irish metro or PoP detail was found.

regions.europe.quote: We manage eight subsea cable systems, are Europe's largest B2B fibre provider and co-own the most widely peered network in the world.
regions.europe.note: Europe is Colt's core delivery region. Own-fibre metro networks across major European cities, 32,000+ buildings and 1,100+ data centres connected, offices in Amsterdam, Barcelona, Brussels, Lisbon, Copenhagen, Frankfurt, Madrid, Paris, Milan, Sibiu, Stockholm, Vienna and Zurich. Note a framing conflict left unresolved: the Our story page says Colt connects 40+ countries, while the Why Colt page says "From our small beginnings in London in 1992, we've grown to over 60 offices in 32 countries." Both figures are recorded as published.

regions.north_america.quote: With Colt fibre and millions more available via our Colt Network as a Service platform across Europe, Asia and the US.
regions.north_america.note: The US is named explicitly as one of three NaaS platform regions on both the SD-WAN page and the networking hub. Corroborated by a Jersey City office and, on the Capital Markets page, transatlantic subsea connectivity into New Jersey and New York. Graded yes for the US specifically. No Canadian or Mexican coverage, PoP or customer evidence was found, so treat the grade as US-centric rather than pan-North-American. The US footprint reads as financial-district and data-centre focused rather than broad national metro fibre.

regions.asia_pacific.quote: We needed a partner who could provide a secure global network to support our expansion. Colt's expertise & reliability helped us connect our operations across Japan, Europe & the US.
regions.asia_pacific.note: Quote is Marc Carbones Gironella, Technology Director, Towa International, on the Pharma page. Asia is one of the three named NaaS platform regions. Corroborated by offices in Tokyo, Osaka, Singapore, Hong Kong, Seoul, Bangalore and Gurgaon; by All Nippon Airways, J Sports Corporation, TV Asahi and Air Internet Service as named Japanese customers; by a Nextrade partnership in Korea on the Capital Markets page; and by independent trade reporting of Arthur D. Little's Singapore and Tokyo offices being migrated onto Colt's network. Japan is clearly the strongest APAC market. No Australia or New Zealand evidence was found.

regions.middle_east_africa.quote: Colt plans to expand its team and continue building its business in its existing markets including Turkey and Dubai.
regions.middle_east_africa.note: Middle East only, and partly forward-looking. Colt's February 2026 announcement confirms existing markets in Turkey and Dubai and leased capacity in three subsea systems crossing the region (Europe India Gateway, FALCON, HAWK). Wider Gulf coverage is explicitly partner-dependent and future tense: "Colt also plans to partner with local operators in markets including Saudi Arabia and additional regions of the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman." No sub-Saharan or North African delivery evidence of any kind was found, so the Africa half of this region is unevidenced. A buyer needing Africa should treat this as unknown.

regions.latin_america.quote: one of the first financial extranet providers to offer access to B3 from all of its 30+ Global PrizmNet PoPs
regions.latin_america.note: The only Latin America evidence found is a 2021 capital markets announcement extending PrizmNet extranet access to Brazil's B3 exchange. Read carefully, this describes reaching a Brazilian venue from Colt's existing global PoPs, not Colt PoPs or fibre inside Latin America. There is no Latin American office on the contact page, and Latin America is not named on the SD-WAN page, the networking hub or the Our story page. This is not evidence that Colt delivers SD-WAN or SASE to enterprise sites in Latin America. Graded partial to reflect a genuine but narrow capital-markets-only reach; the source is five years old.

regions.china_mainland.quote: available directly from within Hong Kong Stock Exchange's (HKEX) colocation facility
regions.china_mainland.note: No evidence of licensed mainland China service delivery was found. Colt lists a Shanghai office on its contact page, but an office is not delivery. The only mainland China product evidence is a 2021 market data announcement adding seven mainland exchanges (SSE, SZSE, CFFEX, ZCE, SHFE, DCE, INE), and that page states the feeds are consumed from within HKEX colocation in Hong Kong or away via the PrizmNet extranet, which is delivery from outside the mainland. The SD-WAN page's footprint claim names only Europe, Asia and the US, with no China-specific licence, partner or PoP statement. Treat the generic global and Asia claims as evidence of nothing for mainland China.

organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.quote: 18/25 of the top global banks trust us with their critical infrastructure and connectivity
organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.note: Colt runs a dedicated Enterprise segment page with named large-enterprise customers (Berlinale, Decathlon, Huisman, France Televisions) and cites G2000 statistics as its framing. The INEOS story records 128 managed sites globally for a group operating 194 facilities in 29 countries, which is a genuinely large multinational deployment. Network scale supports it: "We connect 40+ countries, 32,000 enterprise buildings, 275+ points of presence, and 12 cable landing stations." This is unambiguously Colt's primary segment.

organisation_fit.mid_market.note: Colt publishes a dedicated mid-market segment page at /solutions/business-type/growth headed "Mid-market and high-growth enterprises", with the positioning line "Fast growth brings big demands. We've got the people and expertise to help you build and manage the secure, scalable infrastructure you need." It cites "$67m Average it budget for mid-market customers by 2030 - nearly 5% of revenue" and lists named customers of that scale: Esade, Air Internet Service Co., Ltd, Berlinale, Wempe, Classik Hotel Collection, Altares, CoStar Group and Arthur D. Little. Explicit targeting plus a named customer set meets the test.

organisation_fit.small_business.note: No small business or SME targeting found. Colt's business-type segmentation covers Enterprise, Mid-market and high-growth, and Wholesale; the smallest named segment is mid-market, which is the quoted string. No SMB product tier, no self-serve purchase path and no SME case study were located on colt.net. The only published price point, the G-Cloud 14 figure of "£178 to £451 a unit a month", is a managed per-unit enterprise price rather than an SMB one. Recorded as unknown rather than not_primary because Colt nowhere explicitly states that small business is out of scope; the absence of any SMB tier is the finding, not a stated exclusion.

published_pricing.note: The quoted figure is the only published price found anywhere for Colt SD-WAN: the G-Cloud 14 unit price on the UK Crown Commercial Service Digital Marketplace, for a fully managed service whose "Service wrapper includes design, deployment, configuration, site activation, monitoring" with 24/7 support and four-hour critical response. Nothing is published on colt.net itself; the product page routes to "Contact us" and "Talk to an expert". Graded premium on the combination of that per-unit range, the mandatory managed wrap, own-fibre tier-one carrier positioning, and segmentation that starts at mid-market with no SMB tier. Honest caveat: the £178 entry point sits in mid territory and only the upper end is clearly premium, so a mid grade is defensible from the same evidence. This is a Netify assessment derived from a vendor-submitted framework price, not a vendor positioning statement. Also note the price is a UK public sector framework rate and may not represent commercial enterprise pricing in other regions.

conflicts.claim_a: The Colt IQ Network connects more than 1000+ data centres and over 29,000 on net buildings across Europe
